beats.narration_en: Why is this truck holding a giant blade up at the sky?
It's carrying a wind turbine blade up a mountain road.
Lying flat a blade this long can't get around these bends.
So the trailer tilts it up as steep as sixty degrees.
At that angle it sticks out only half as far.
And it can swing the blade sideways to clear cliffs and trees.
Some of these blades are almost as long as a football field.
The truck crawls along at about twelve miles an hour.
And if the wind blows over twenty miles an hour the trip stops.
Tilting the blade means the mountain roads don't have to be rebuilt.
That's why you might meet a wind turbine blade pointing at the sky.
